title: Delete the Half-Good Things
author: Scott D. Clary
summary: Clary observes that genuinely effective people are doing less, not more. The difference is not in ambition but in ruthlessness about the things that stay. Watch someone at peace and in command: they have fewer meetings, fewer goals, fewer tabs open, fewer obligations. This isn't slacking; it's discipline. The trap is the half-good thing: the decent opportunity, the useful meeting, the achievable goal, the safe bet. All of those individually sound rational, but together they create drowning. High performers don't say no to bad things; they say no to okay things so that great things get all the oxygen. This is the hardest decision in leadership because the things you cut are not failures, they are just not worth your scarce resource of focus.
points: Effective people are not more ambitious; they are ruthlessly ambitious about fewer things.
The trap is the half-good opportunity: decent, useful, achievable, but together they create drowning.
High performers say no to okay things so that the great things get all the oxygen and attention.
It is harder to cut a decent thing than a bad thing because the decent thing has a logical argument for staying.
Focus is your scarcest resource; every decent thing you keep is focus stolen from something greater.
quotes: Watch someone who's genuinely happy and effective. Not performing happiness on Instagram. Actually peaceful. Actually productive. They're doing less than you.
Fewer meetings. Fewer goals. Fewer tabs open. Fewer obligations. Fewer things competing for their attention.

This isn't because they're less ambitious. They're ruthlessly ambitious about fewer things. And that's exactly why they're winning while you're drowning.” Archived from Scott D. Clary Newsletter on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
